pr_title: Let `openssl crl` support the use of engines.
pr_comments: fixed the unhandled OPT_ENGINE in switch warning and all the other problems are unrelated to my changes.  Please review and if appropriate pull into master.
At least the `check_docs` failure is relevant

> At least the `check_docs` failure is relevant

Indeed it is!! I'll get that fixed up.
It is fairly ugly to add an option to a command and immediately deprecate it. IMO this should be discussed in OTC.
OTC: Engines can be loaded via the config file if needed. Engines are deprecated in 3.0 and therefore we will not be adding any further support.

Thanks for all the work in thinking about this.  

Note that 1.1.1 will get support as LTS  until 2023.  Presumably, that means that the next LTS branch will be cut in 2022; about a year from now.  I'm going to assume engines will not be removed by 2022 as that would be a massive undertaking because providers would have to take over everything, so that means the next LTS will likely have engine support.  If that branch is cut in 2022 and LTSs live for 5 years, you're letting this command-line inconsistency live until 2027. Does that really seem like a good idea to the OMC? 

The answer is likely yes and I'm fine with it.  Just wanted to make this timeline  a bit more explicit.

The next LTS will be based on some version from 3.0 onwards. 3.0 deprecates all engines and they are not encouraged for use. Of course that does mean engines will still *exist* for some time to come - but we do expect that usage to be reducing. We are comfortable living with some inconsistencies until they are finally removed.

review_comments: I see this call without #ifdef in other apps...

`setup_engine()` will get your engine registered.  Then when you go to use algorithms your pmeth's and ameth's in your engine can  be selected.  You might think this looks strange, but if you grep for `engine` in the follow apps code files you'll see my engine code is similar to them. 

- x509.c
- srp.c
- verify.c
- pkey.c 
- rsautl.c
....and many others.

> I see this call without #ifdef in other apps...

I was just following what `OPENSSL_NO_MD5` ....if I follow that, it looks nicer and has less cognitive load.
